title: Steady-State Endurance Run - 90 Minutes (Engelbrektsloppet Prep)

items.name: Cat-Cow
items.cues: Move slowly and deliberately, synchronizing breath with movement. Arch on inhale, round on exhale. Activate core throughout.

items.name: Bird Dog
items.cues: Extend opposite arm and leg while maintaining a neutral spine. Pause briefly at full extension. Keep movements controlled and balanced.

items.name: 90/90 Hip Switches
items.cues: Rotate hips smoothly between positions, maintaining upright posture. Focus on hip mobility and preparation for running mechanics.

items.name: Easy Jogging
items.cues: Build heart rate gradually. Stay conversational - you should be able to speak in full sentences. Focus on relaxed, efficient cadence.

items.name: Steady-State Running - Phase 1
items.cues: Maintain RPE 5-6 (conversational pace). Focus on consistent breathing pattern - try 3-4 steps per breath. Relax shoulders, keep arms at 90 degrees. Monitor for steady effort without strain.

items.name: Steady-State Running - Phase 2
items.cues: Continue same pace and intensity. Mid-workout mental checkpoint: assess breathing ease, leg fatigue level, and hydration needs. Maintain discipline - do not accelerate beyond target RPE.

items.name: Steady-State Running - Phase 3 (Final Push)
items.cues: Maintain RPE 5-6 for final segment. Legs may feel fatigue - this is normal. Focus on form: upright posture, steady cadence, controlled breathing. You are building aerobic base for 45km race.

items.name: Easy Walking
items.cues: Gradually reduce intensity. Walk at easy pace, allow heart rate to drop naturally. Focus on steady breathing and recovery.

items.name: Calf Stretch
items.cues: Hold each side 30 seconds. Keep heel planted, lean forward gently. No bouncing - static stretch only.

items.name: Biceps Wall Stretch
items.cues: Hold each arm 30 seconds. Place palm on wall at shoulder height, gently turn away. Feel stretch in front of shoulder.

items.name: Cat-Cow
items.cues: Slow, controlled movements to mobilize spine post-run. Synchronize with breath for relaxation and recovery.

rationale: At 20 days out from Engelbrektsloppet 45km, building aerobic endurance base is critical. 90-minute steady-state run at RPE 5-6 develops aerobic capacity and race-specific fatigue adaptation without excess injury risk.

Recent training shows strong recovery with 'great' status. User has completed multiple endurance sessions; this workout builds on that foundation with appropriate duration matching the target 90-minute slot.

RPE 5-6 intensity is sustainable for long-duration training, promoting fat oxidation and aerobic development while preserving nervous system recovery. No injuries reported, allowing full running volume.
